title: Free Printable Coloring Pages - 300 DPI PDF Downloads | Printable Coloring Pages
excerpt: Free printable coloring pages as true 1-bit vector PDFs at 300 DPI, sized for both US Letter and A4. Every page is measured, print-tested on real inkjet and laser printers and reviewed by a human. No signup, no watermark.
content_html:
Printable coloring pages that actually print right.

2,308 free coloring pages. True 300 DPI, true 1-bit vector PDFs, laid out for US Letter and A4 - no scaling, no grey fringes, no signup.

Every page is free to download, print-tested on real printers, and yours to use commercially.

True 300 DPI vector PDF US Letter and A4 No signup, no watermarks

Can't find it? Draw it.

Describe it and we draw it, in exactly the same format as everything else here: true 1-bit line art, a real vector PDF, US Letter and A4 at 300 DPI.

Free, no signup. Public-domain and original generic designs only - no trademarked characters.

For developers

The whole library, as a JSON API

Search, metadata and direct PDF, PNG and SVG URLs for every page - public domain, so your users never owe attribution. Free key, 500 requests a day.

Get a free API key 

curl "https://printablecoloringpages.ai/api/pages/search?q=owl&key=YOUR_KEY"

Frequently asked questions

Yes. Every page is a free download in PDF, PNG and SVG - no trial, no daily cap, no watermark and no account. They are released into the public domain under CC0, so classroom, church, library and commercial use are all fine.

Because it is a true 1-bit vector PDF, not a compressed photo of line art. There is no grey anywhere in the file, so nothing turns muddy on a laser printer, and the lines stay sharp at any size.

Both, for every single page, laid out separately for each printable box. You never have to scale, shrink-to-fit or crop, which is what causes the grey border and the clipped edges people get elsewhere.

24 lb / 90 gsm or heavier. Plain 20 lb / 80 gsm copier paper is fine for pencils and crayons but alcohol markers will bleed through it. Pages that have tight gaps between lines say so on the page itself.

No, deliberately. Everything here is public-domain or an original generic design, so a teacher, a childminder or a small business can print it without a licensing question hanging over it.

Yes. Submit your SVG at Printable Coloring Pages/submit/ and, once reviewed, it gets its own page, free hosting, PDF + PNG + SVG downloads, and full credit with a link back to you.

Artists: share your line art

Drew something you want in the public domain? Upload the SVG and it joins the library under your name, with the print-ready PDFs generated for you.

Submit a page
